newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - RTZ-CRA sees Kennecott resolved.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - RTZ-CRA sees Kennecott resolved.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Thursday that it had solved most of the problems at its Kennecott copper smelter in the United States.
"You have got most of the problems solved," chief executive Leon Davis told a news conference.
"We are down to virtually the last section of the smelter. We have squeezed them (the problems) out and hopefully once we have squeezed this they have all gone," Davis said.
The company said the remaining problems were to increase capacity from the anode refining furnaces and redesign the casting wheel arrangement.

"Whilst we have had a problematic year, over the last few months we have seen a significant improvement in the performance out of the smelter and also we have seen a notable reduction in the number of the problems we have been facing," executive chairman Robert Wilson said.
"So we believe that the major problems that adversely affected our earnings last year are going to be tackled fairly substantially ... this year," Wilson said.
RTZ-CRA said the planned six week shut-down of the smelter will still go ahead.

The Anglo-Australian mining giant specifically referred to problems at the Kennecott smelter as a partial explanation for its fall in calendar 1996 net profit to US$1.096 billion from US$1.441 billion in 1995.
The company said the Kennecott Metals group's net profit fell to US$148 million in 1996 from US$439 million in 1995.
It has previously said that it planned to shut part of the smelter for six weeks for major modification work. This would occur in the first half of 1997.
